summary: New idiom: ʕwəǧle/ʕowəǧ darbo 'vom geraden Weg abweichen, hier: ehelich untreu werden'

data.headword: ʕwəǧle/ʕowəǧ darbo 'vom geraden Weg abweichen, hier: ehelich untreu werden'
data.turoyo: faqaṭ ramḥəl, me d hawina aṯto w gawro, d oṯe naqla d ʕuǧo u darbo, ġer mu qaṭlo layt bayn luno w liya!
data.translation: aber wenn wir Morgen Mann und Frau geworden sind, und es dann vorkommt, daß sie noch einmal vom geraden Wege abweicht, dann gibt es nur töten zwischen mir und ihr!

rationale: One clear inherited collocation, already marked with an idiom question; index it without a duplicate boxed example.

summary: Active I physical bending contrasts with Detransitive tilting/state. The latter has no overt agent in the truck, finger or wood contexts; curved plough wood may simply be a static shape, without an asserted prior bending event.
The active 26/253 construction takes direct u darbo, whereas the inherited Detransitive route example has m-u=darbo. They should not be collapsed into one government pattern.

ʕwiǧo is already the inherited Detransitive Part. Pass. citation form. Explicit qayso in the plough context supports a nominally modifying state reading; the injured-finger referent has a less secure agreement analysis.
Two inherited Detransitive senses are now numbered for publication: physical deformation/state and route turning. This organizes existing examples and leaves active I.1 unchanged.
Lookup ʕuǧo found only the already quoted 26/253 example, and ʕwiǧo found the plough excerpt under ʔṣr; no separate path idiom was already listed.

In Lahdo snake/8, does ʕwiǧo modify a masculine understood finger, represent a lexical state form, or a finite feminine Detransitive Preterit? Preserve the attested state filing until agreement is confirmed.
Does ʕwǧ u darbo conventionally imply marital infidelity, or broader moral deviation? The single inherited context supplies the marital interpretation.
